runners_data.name: Time For The Moon
runners_data.comment: Boasts a win three starts back and a third four starts back on today's going, though two unplaced efforts since give slight pause; back after 18 days, the top-rated colt looks the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Apulia Bay
runners_data.comment: Twice placed in his last two starts, Apulia Bay brings strong fitness at 14 days, experience on today's going, and a yard firing at 26% — though yet to score in recent starts, that's the one knock against him here.

runners_data.name: Free World
runners_data.note: A hold-up operator who stays 2m on good ground (7 runs, 1W1P on similar), but a repeated fading tendency in the finish is a significant concern for a race likely run at a controlled tempo with a premium on the closing kick.
runners_data.comment: Free World won last time out and, having run over today's trip and going, he can go well again just seven days on from that win — the one to beat here, with our rating of 67 giving him a narrow edge over his five rivals.

runners_data.name: Joanna Hiffernan
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed pace-setter; Jack Callan rides for Owen Burrows who is in modest 14-day form (1/10), but the tactical advantage of owning the lead in a field of closers on good-to-firm is enormous over this marathon trip.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, with a pair of fourths and a sixth before finishing second last time out, Joanna Hiffernan has going experience in her favour but looks held on our figures as the bottom-ranked runner in the field.

runners_data.name: Hope Rising
runners_data.note: Jamie Snowden's filly has an excellent record at extreme distances on good ground (4W9P from 15 similar-going runs) and as the only prominent racer she is best placed to track Joanna Hiffernan and apply pressure in the straight; Harry Vigors takes 3lb.
runners_data.comment: Hope Rising arrives on the back of a win last time out and has experience of today's going, giving her a strong fitness and conditions profile — the chief concern is whether she can defy a mark of 55 off 141 lb on the back of a quick turnaround.

runners_data.name: Simiyann
runners_data.note: Ian Williams runner with a blinkered headgear entry; in reality a hold-up horse whose placement in midfield on the map reflects overcrowding at the rear — with STYLE_FIT at 0.91, his chance is meaningfully tempered by the likelihood he cannot settle where he needs to in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Simiyann has been knocking on the door, finishing third last time out and a second two starts back, and he returns on a quick turnaround over familiar distance and going — the chief concern is that he remains winless in recent starts despite his consistent placing.

runners_data.name: Zooter
runners_data.note: A three-year-old hold-up type stepping up markedly in trip to 2m having been raced mainly at 8-10f; Connor Planas takes the mount and while the step to this extreme distance is an unknown, he carries only 132lbs and a strong late run is his only path.
runners_data.comment: Zooter has been knocking on the door with a third last time out, and a second five starts back confirms he knows how to get involved; he has run over today's going before and returns fit on 16 days' rest. The risk is that he remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Assured
runners_data.note: Tom Gretton's gelding wears a hood and is winless in nine comparable-going starts; his true hold-up style has been displaced to midfield on the map due to field composition, and with STYLE_FIT flagging he is unlikely to race where he needs to — his OR of 48 also marks him as the least exposed runner on ratings.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Assured faces a stiff task here; she has experience of today's going and arrives reasonably fresh at 27 days since her last run, but those are slim threads to cling to.

races.paceDynamic: Joanna Hiffernan is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner field over two miles on good-to-firm ground at Nottingham, and with no other genuine pace-setter to challenge her, she is set to control proceedings at whatever tempo she chooses from the outset. The remainder of the field — Free World, Simiyann, Zooter, and Assured — are all hold-up types by nature, meaning Joanna Hiffernan can dictate a comfortable, measured gallop that keeps them bottled up behind her for the majority of the trip. Hope Rising, a prominent racer with strong form at extreme distances, is the only runner likely to apply any meaningful pressure closer to the pace, and the two miles on fast ground suits her stamina profile well. Simiyann and Assured are genuine hold-up horses whose natural rear-positioning style has been redistributed to midfield on the map — in this race shape, one dominated by a lone front-runner, they are unlikely to secure the ground-saving position they need, and the race strongly favours the prominent runner Hope Rising and any hold-up horse with the finishing speed to close on a leader who hasn't been harassed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Joanna Hiffernan Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Joanna Hiffernan settles into an uncontested lead and dictates a comfortable gallop throughout, she builds a cushion that proves too great for the hold-up horses to reel in.
scenarios.body: With no rival willing or able to press her early, she controls every yard and can quicken when she chooses in the straight, leaving the closers with too much ground to make up on fast ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hope Rising Tracks And Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Hope Rising travels prominently just off Joanna Hiffernan's shoulder and uses superior stamina to wear her down in the final quarter-mile.
scenarios.body: Hope Rising's form over 16-18f on good ground is excellent and she was placed in both her most recent starts at extreme trips, suggesting she has the engine to sustain an effort from the front group into the closing stages.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swamp The Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Joanna Hiffernan goes too hard early or the pace is stronger than expected and the field closes rapidly in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Free World and Zooter, both genuine hold-up types, would be the chief beneficiaries if the pace collapses, though Free World's noted tendency to fade at the finish tempers confidence.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Runners Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Simiyann or Assured, both mapped out of their natural rear positions, somehow secure a more forward berth and produce a sustained run from midfield.
scenarios.body: Both carry STYLE_FIT flags of 0.91 indicating they are racing out of role, and their recent form — particularly Assured's zero wins in nine starts on comparable going — makes this a low-probability outcome.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Hope Rising is sent forward immediately to track Joanna Hiffernan — if Harry Vigors elects to race prominently from the start rather than settling in midfield, she becomes the most dangerous rival to the leader by a considerable margin.

Joanna Hiffernan's true gallop in the opening mile is critical — if Jack Callan is allowed to dawdle into the straight with a field of closers, she could slow the pace to a crawl and then sprint clear, making the hold-up horses' finishing kicks irrelevant.

Free World's documented tendency to fade late is a significant flag on good-to-firm ground over 2m; back Free World's positioning but be cautious of its resolution if the race develops into a sustained sprint from the two-furlong pole.

Simiyann and Assured both carry redistribution tags — monitor their actual race positions at the early stages; if either does manage to find a forward berth against expectation, the scenario probabilities shift meaningfully toward Scenario D.

Zooter's trip extension to 2m is uncharted — watch early how Connor Planas settles him, as a horse habitually racing over a mile who finds the pace too searching could weaken dramatically in the final half-mile on fast ground.

races.name: Oddschecker Free Bets Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Beauty Generation
runners_data.note: Five-year-old stepping back up to 10f, where its three wins at the trip and a recent 3rd on Good give genuine distance and going credentials; naturally a hold-up horse but the glut of closers in this field means it is likely to race closer to midfield than it would prefer, tempering its chance in a true sit-and-sprint shape.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out and a winner two starts back, Beauty Generation brings some fair recent form to the table, and he has run over today's trip and going before; 136 lb is a hefty burden from stall seven, however, and his inconsistency in recent starts is a concern.

runners_data.name: Daretobedifferent
runners_data.note: Holds a win over 8f on Good and has finished in the frame six times in fifteen Good-ground starts, bringing the clearest recent form to today; pressed into the pace-setting role by the absence of any confirmed front-runner, which is contrary to its natural instinct, so its stamina for 10f at this likely tempo is the key question.

runners_data.name: Diane Chasseresse
runners_data.note: Owen Burrows filly with only three runs to her name and a modest 656 form string that offers little encouragement; all three runs have been over shorter trips than today's 1m2f and she has not placed yet, making the step up in trip and competition a significant ask without obvious pace preference.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts, with a run of sixths and a fifth telling a consistent story of mid-pack mediocrity, Diane Chasseresse arrives 29 days fresh but our figures rank her last of eight, and going experience offers little comfort when the form reads this poorly.

runners_data.name: Bradbury
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's three-year-old carries the strongest recent trainer form (7/28 in 14 days) and has shown versatility in form figures, including a 2nd and a 1st; natural closer shuffled toward midfield in a field full of hold-up types, and the headgear note (t/ce) suggests connections have been working to sharpen its focus — a horse whose chance depends on securing a clean run in the straight.
runners_data.comment: Bradbury arrives on a sharp 16-day turnaround with two wins in his last six starts, third last time out keeping him in fine form, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions — the main risk is whether 132 lb from stall 1 blunts his finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Tommo's Ginjaninja
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason partners this Easterby-trained three-year-old returning from 57 days off, which is the longest break in the field and a potential fitness concern on a sharp track; a genuine late-runner by nature, it has been mapped to midfield because there is no room at the rear, and any freshness-related sluggishness early could leave it with an impossible task.
runners_data.comment: Tommo's Ginjaninja showed real promise with a second and a third in recent starts, and he has experience over today's trip and going — our rating has him joint-top of this field. The risk is two below-par efforts since, including a ninth last time out after 57 days off.

runners_data.name: The Anthony Gover
runners_data.note: Newland & Insole's runner has not placed in six recent starts with three finishes last in seven-furlong races suggesting the 10f step may suit, but its Going History (hg:p) indicates a possible preference for softer ground than today's Good to Firm; another natural hold-up horse squeezed into midfield and carrying a 0/6 record over the relevant going conditions.
runners_data.comment:
Winless in his last six starts, The Anthony Gover does at least bring going experience and a rating of 66 that edges his official mark — third on the list six starts back offers hope he retains ability, but consistency remains the concern.

Wait - let me recount: 6th(1), 4th(2), 6th(3), unplaced(4), 6th(5), 3rd(6). The 3rd is SIX starts back.

runners_data.name: Midnight Media
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand takes the ride for the Muir & Grassick stable which has hit 3/23 in the last fortnight; the form string includes back-to-back placed efforts (2nd and 1st over 10f and 8f on Tapeta/turf) suggesting the trip is fine, and Marquand's ability to time a run makes this one of the most interesting horses mapped to midfield in a compressed field.
runners_data.comment: Midnight Media won two starts back and has been placed either side of that success, showing she's competitive at this level, but a ninth four starts back hints at inconsistency; she has distance and going experience and a decent weight pull could help from stall 4.

runners_data.name: Katalyst
runners_data.note: Stablemate of Midnight Media under the same yard (Muir & Grassick) with Ryan Kavanagh claiming 3lbs, which partially offsets the OR=60 burden; the headgear note (hg:b) — blinkers — suggests a need for sharpening, and while two placed efforts at 9-10f on Good ground are encouraging, the 13th and 10th on Polytrack are a concern if any bounce factor is in play after 15 days.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, with two unplaced efforts sandwiched between modest placings, Katalyst faces a stiff task ranked seventh of eight on our figures, though she has run over today's distance and going before and returns on a quick 15-day turnaround.

races.paceDynamic: Daretobedifferent is the sole confirmed pace-setter here, redistributed to the front from a natural hold-up style but still the most likely horse to show early — on Good to Firm ground over 1m2f at Nottingham, that means a single uncontested gallop is almost certain, with no rival capable of applying sustained early pressure. The pace will be honest rather than scorching, set by one horse who does not relish making it alone, which typically produces a strongly-run final quarter-mile on this flat track that rewards horses with a genuine finishing kick. The field is overwhelmingly stacked with hold-up types — Beauty Generation, Bradbury, Tommo's Ginjaninja, The Anthony Gover, Midnight Media and Katalyst are all natural closers — but there are simply too many to find genuine room at the rear, meaning several will be squeezed into midfield positions that do not play to their strengths. This race shape, with one front-runner and a wall of closers, should produce a fairly genuine test that favours horses able to travel in midfield and pick up over the final two furlongs; pure hold-up horses dependent on a fast pace may find the lone leader's tempo too comfortable.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Daretobedifferent crosses unchallenged and sets a controlled, even tempo that allows it to coast into the straight with energy reserves.
scenarios.body: Daretobedifferent dictates from the front without any pressure, builds a steady lead and may simply outstay rivals who struggle to find their rhythm from awkward midfield positions; the Good to Firm surface suits a measured gallop that keeps the pace honest without burning the leader out.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Runners Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the steady pace compresses the field and two or three midfield horses peel wide in the straight with room to finish strongly.
scenarios.body: Horses redistributed into midfield — Midnight Media, Bradbury and Katalyst — get close enough to the pace to launch a challenge in the final two furlongs without needing the extreme late burst that a true hold-up run demands; the flat Nottingham straight and good ground reward sustained finishing acceleration from mid-division.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Swamp Leader Late
scenarios.trigger: If Daretobedifferent sets a pace fractionally too strong early and fades inside the final furlong, opening the door for natural hold-up runners.
scenarios.body: The genuine deep closers — Beauty Generation, Tommo's Ginjaninja, The Anthony Gover — would need a fast enough tempo to set up a strong late run, which is unlikely given Daretobedifferent's natural reluctance to front-run at a true gallop; this scenario is discounted because so many hold-up types are racing out of role and cannot rely on a pace that may never truly materialise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If the controlled pace is so forgiving that Daretobedifferent simply has too much in reserve and the backmarkers cannot close the gap in time.
scenarios.body: With no pressure and a comfortable early sectional, Daretobedifferent may simply find its rivals have ridden too conservatively, leaving too much to do over Nottingham's shorter run-in; this is the lowest-probability shape given the horse is racing out of role and lacks the confirmed front-running profile to dominate from the front.

watchPoints.text: Daretobedifferent — watch whether Marco Ghiani elects to stride on or attempts to slot in; if it leads by default it is racing outside its comfort zone and any signs of laboured jumping off the bridle early could signal the field bunching and causing traffic interference through the midfield pack.

Tommo's Ginjaninja — the 57-day layoff is the longest in the field and on a Good to Firm surface that will test fitness from the first furlong; watch for signs of greenness or sluggishness leaving the stalls that could compromise its chance before the race has even settled.

Midnight Media and Katalyst — both run for Muir & Grassick and both are likely to be ridden from hold-up positions in the same part of the track; watch whether they interfere with each other's run or whether Tom Marquand and Kavanagh are forced to split their paths, which on a flat one-bend track could cost one or both horses vital ground.

Bradbury — the addition of tongue-tie and cheekpieces (hg:t/ce) is worth monitoring in the paddock; if the headgear switch visibly settles it pre-race it may travel more smoothly in midfield, but if it overreacts it could find itself further back than ideal in a field where the front is barely contested.

races.name: Oddschecker+ Subscription Service Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Grandlad
runners_data.note: Front-runner with a recent 5f win on Good going and solid sim-going record (3W5P), but the presence of Goyard ensures he will not be gifted a soft lead — his ability to sustain after a fight for the front is the key question at a 17-day return.
runners_data.comment: Grandlad won three starts back and has experience of today's trip and conditions, returning fit on 17 days off carrying 133 lb from stall one — the risk is that his last two runs have seen him finish sixth and seventh.

runners_data.name: Goyard
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner trained by the in-form David O'Meara (T14: 7/52) who will likely send him forward hard, though his record shows more places than wins on Good ground and he has not won over 5f recently; contested pace scenarios may drain him before the line.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Goyard did show a third three starts back and returns here 16 days on from a fourth, with experience over today's trip and going a steadying factor; 132 lb from stall two is the challenge.

runners_data.name: Jax Edge
runners_data.note: Gina Mangan takes the ride on this prominent-style 6yo who has form showing a 6f Nottingham win on Good ground; he tracks pace well and his sim-going record of 2W5P from 11 runs suggests he handles this surface reliably — prominent position suits perfectly here.
runners_data.comment: Ranked last on our figures and her recent form makes grim reading — eighth and seventh in her last two starts — though she does own a win in her last six and has run over today's distance and going before. Hard to fancy at 130 lb.

runners_data.name: Forager
runners_data.note: An 81-day break is significant context; despite being a genuine hold-up horse by style, the compressed field created by two front-runners means he is unlikely to find the gap he needs, and his sim-going record of 3W3P was built in less congested circumstances — style fit is compromised in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Beaten well into the rear on her last two starts and 81 days between runs counts against her, though she does own a win three starts back and has run over today's trip and going before. Hard to fancy ranked sixth of seven on our figures.

runners_data.name: Mesaafi
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and is a natural closer, but with Forager also pushing into the midfield zone, Mesaafi's ability to find clear running from his natural position is undermined; his most recent runs show a string of disappointing efforts and only one win in his last five on Good ground.
runners_data.comment: Mesaafi ran over today's trip and going combination and a win four starts back underlines his capability at this level, with a rating of 86 supporting his claims from stall five; the main risk is his two latest runs have both been unplaced.

runners_data.name: Michaela's Boy
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner at OR=87 carrying 140lbs for Robert Cowell (T14: 1/12) and a genuine hold-up type with a 5f win on Good ground; Marco Ghiani is an experienced rider who can place him well, though the weight burden and hold-up style in a compressed race shape are notable headwinds.
runners_data.comment: Michaela's Boy was a winner one start back and has experience of today's trip and conditions; drawn in stall six carrying 140 lb, the eighth last time out is the one query, though his rating of 89 marks him as the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Moulin Booj
runners_data.note: Consistent placer on Good 5f turf (1W5P in sim-going, multiple 2nds and 3rds recently) with Tom Marquand taking the ride for a trainer with 2 from 14 in the past fortnight; hold-up by style but his consistent closing form gives him each-way viability if the pace burns out the leaders.
runners_data.comment: Moulin Booj has finished second twice in his last six starts — most recently last time out and three starts back — and returns fit on just ten days' rest, with experience of today's distance and going telling in his favour; the concern is that he remains yet to win in recent starts.

races.paceDynamic: Grandlad and Goyard are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead aggressively from the Nottingham 5f gates, creating a genuinely contested early pace on ground that is riding Good to Firm throughout the card. With two horses intent on the same piece of real estate at the head of affairs, the gallop will be honest to strong rather than artificially dawdled, meaning the front two will be burning energy from the off. This race shape — fast-run, flat 5f on quick ground — historically favours horses that can sit just off a contested lead and sustain their effort through the final furlong rather than true sit-and-sprint hold-up horses, making the prominent/just-off-pace profile the primary tactical beneficiary. The field contains more hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear: Forager and Mesaafi are genuine closers but have been redistributed to midfield in the map because the limited ground behind a contested early pace compresses the field, meaning neither will enjoy the clear-passage late run their style demands.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead Burns Them
scenarios.trigger: If Grandlad and Goyard fight hard for the lead and set a strong pace that softens both, a horse sitting just off the pace in the prominent position conserves energy to strike.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners empty each other's tanks through the first three furlongs on fast ground, leaving a gap for a prominent stalker to pick up the pieces entering the final furlong; Jax Edge, with strong course-form over 5f-6f at Nottingham on this going and proven ability to track a strong pace, is ideally placed in this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Grandlad breaks sharply and Goyard is content to sit off rather than fight for the lead, a lone front-runner dictates a controlled pace and holds on.
scenarios.body: With a solo lead and no rival to run him ragged, Grandlad can control fractions and conserve enough to last home on going that suits him; his Good-ground 5f record includes a recent win on this going type and his trainer has Kaiya Fraser on board specifically for this assignment.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly extreme and the field spreads wide, creating an opening for closers to finish strongly down the outside.
scenarios.body: Michaela's Boy carries top weight at OR=87 but has a genuine win over 5f on Good ground and is the most credible hold-up runner not hampered by redistribution concerns; Moulin Booj's consistent placed form on Good 5f suggests he can thread through a tiring field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If one or both front-runners miss the break or check stride, disrupting the anticipated pace dynamic entirely.
scenarios.body: Without a genuine early pace the race becomes a tactical sprint from halfway, favouring horses with raw finishing speed on fast ground regardless of style; Moulin Booj's series of placings on Good 5f turf makes him the most consistent beneficiary of an unstructured dash.

watchPoints.text: Grandlad and Goyard — watch which of them actually wins the early battle for the lead at the off; if Goyard forces Grandlad to race at maximum effort in the first furlong, both could be spent before the final 100 yards and the race opens up dramatically for the stalkers.

Jax Edge — Gina Mangan is a 3lb claimer; watch for any position issues leaving the stalls as Nottingham's 5f shoot requires a clean, balanced break to secure a prominent pitch before the field narrows.

Forager's 81-day absence — horses returning after 11+ weeks to a fast-paced 5f handicap often need the run, and if he is short of peak fitness his hold-up style offers no early safety net; watch the market for any significant drift.

Moulin Booj — Tom Marquand's booking for a George Scott horse often signals stable confidence; his recent 2nd over this exact trip and going at 5f is the most directly relevant form in the race and warrants monitoring in the show.

Going correction — the going report consistently lists this race as Good to Firm, not Good as declared; fast ground will amplify the cost of fighting for the lead early and may compress finishing times, slightly shortening the margin for hold-up horses to make up ground.

races.name: Oddschecker Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Thunderous Love
runners_data.note: Won twice in this grade and has strong course-distance form on Good ground, but faces a prominent field and is likely to find herself in a tighter tracking position than she ideally wants — her chance is real if she can settle just off the pace, but the [STYLE_FIT] tag reflects the squeeze in the prominent berths; Rob Hornby booking is solid and trainer form at 1/14 over 14 days is moderate.
runners_data.comment: Placed last time out and boasting experience over today's trip and conditions, Thunderous Love arrives in good order just 17 days since her latest run and our rating of 73 marks her out as a lively contender — though she remains winless in recent starts, that runner-up effort suggests she's close to ending that run.

runners_data.name: Melissa Honey
runners_data.note: Boasts an excellent recent form string including two wins over 6f on Good ground and is clearly in form for Michael Herrington, who is running at a respectable 2/11 strike rate; her true role is to close from the back and David Probert will need the pace to be genuine enough in a 6-runner field to make that effective — the small field is her biggest obstacle.
runners_data.comment: Ranked fifth of six on our figures, Melissa Honey faces a stiff ask here, though she does arrive on the back of a third last time out, with a win two starts back offering some encouragement, and she has experience of today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Seeing Stars
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a win to her name over 7f on Standard and solid placed efforts, though her record on turf Good ground is limited at 0W1P from three runs — Marco Ghiani rides and she is well-positioned tactically to stalk Sugar Sugar, but the concern is whether she can sustain her effort over the closing stages given recent fading efforts.
runners_data.comment: Seeing Stars brings strong claims here — third two starts back and a winner five starts back show she handles this trip and going, and 19 days is a fresh, race-ready gap. The risk is that eighth last time out leaves something to prove after that sharp dip in form.

runners_data.name: Sweet Desire
runners_data.note: 58-day absence is a significant red flag, trainer Steph Hollinshead has sent out no winners in 14 days (0/7), the form string reads 0-4-8 and she carries a ⚠ fade-in-finish flag — hold-up style on a fast surface in a small field adds further risk, and she looks best watched rather than opposed on the basis of hope.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked last on our figures, Sweet Desire faces a stiff ask here; an eighth and an unplaced run among her recent efforts make her hard to fancy, though she has run over today's trip before and draws stall one.

runners_data.name: Come On Eibhlin
runners_data.note: Stepping sharply back in trip from 8-10f to 6f, which is a major question mark given her entire form profile is built around staying trips — she has placed three times at 7-10f on Good ground and trainer Dylan Cunha is active (4/28 T14), but the drop to a sharp 6f on quick ground asks a question she may not be able to answer.

runners_data.name: Sugar Sugar
runners_data.note: Won over this exact course, distance, and going at her most recent start and holds prominent early pace — she is the race shaper in every meaningful sense; George Bass takes over from the previous jockey and the /es headgear flag suggests she has been suited by equipment, making her the clearest tactical asset in this small field.
runners_data.comment: Sugar Sugar arrives in cracking nick — a winner last time out and placed in two of her three starts before that — and has run over today's trip and going; the chief concern is her weight of 133 lb.

races.paceDynamic: Sugar Sugar is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with only five rivals in a small 6f field on Good to Firm ground at Nottingham, she is likely to dictate an honest but unchallenged gallop from the outset. Seeing Stars and Thunderous Love are the prominent types who will track her, though Thunderous Love is genuinely being pushed out of its natural berth — it wants to sit closer to the pace than the map shows but faces competition for that position from Seeing Stars. The hold-up runners — Melissa Honey, Sweet Desire, and Come On Eibhlin — will settle in the rear third, with Melissa Honey the most capable of those despite being displaced on the map from her true back-of-field role. With just one front-runner setting a controlled, sustainable tempo on fast ground in a small field, this race shape strongly favours horses with early pace or prominent racing tactics who can travel into the race without burning energy chasing a contested gallop — the hold-up brigade faces the classic small-field closer's dilemma of insufficient cover and an honest but not scorching pace to reel in.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sugar Sugar Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Sugar Sugar leads unchallenged at a controlled tempo and none of the prominent trackers can sustain a challenge over the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Sugar Sugar's last win came over this exact course, distance, and going combination, and uncontested on a fast surface over 6f she can set her own fractions and prove hard to peg back; Seeing Stars is the most natural threat tracking into contention, but her recent form shows a pattern of fading after early effort.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challenger Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Seeing Sugar loses her early fluency or is pressed fractionally harder than expected, allowing a tracking prominent runner to hit the front with momentum entering the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Seeing Stars or Thunderous Love, travelling into a sustainable tempo, would have the tactical advantage of pounceing off the leader's back without having burned reserves — Thunderous Love in particular has recent course-distance form on similar ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Finisher Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is strong enough to stretch the field and create a genuine gap for a hold-up horse to run through late.
scenarios.body: Melissa Honey is the most credentialled finisher in the field with multiple wins and places over 6f on Good ground, and if the pace draws the prominent types off their feet she has the profile to benefit — but the small field and controlled pace make this scenario genuinely unlikely.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Collapse And Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace collapses entirely, the field concertinas and the race becomes a sprint from the 2f pole with no true winner of the shape.
scenarios.body: In this unlikely muddle, finishing speed over the closing stages on fast ground would determine the outcome, and horses with a high TS ceiling like Seeing Stars or Melissa Honey could benefit from a flat-out dash.

watchPoints.text: Sugar Sugar's early jump from the stalls is critical — if she breaks cleanly and crosses to the rail she controls the race entirely; watch for any sluggish start that allows Seeing Stars or Thunderous Love to grab the position she needs.

Thunderous Love will want to race closer than the mapped position suggests — watch for Rob Hornby pushing forward early to avoid being trapped in a pocket in a small 6-runner field, which could create a brief flash of early pressure on Sugar Sugar before settling.

Melissa Honey's chance is entirely conditioned on the pace being strong enough to tire the leaders — in a 6-runner race with one front-runner, watch whether the gallop is genuinely honest or a dawdle, as the latter kills her chance outright.

Come On Eibhlin's market move (if any) should be monitored with scepticism — her entire form profile is over 8-10f and the step back to 6f on fast ground looks risky, with headgear (tb) suggesting connections are experimenting rather than confident.

Sweet Desire's 58-day layoff combined with a trainer who has sent out no winners in 14 days and a known tendency to fade in the finish makes her behaviour in the first furlong instructive — if she travels sweetly early she may run respectably, but she is unlikely to win.
